title: Icarus — What the myth explains
summary: Icarus flew too close to the sun on wax wings made by his father Daedalus. This study reads the myth as an answer to a question.
body:
Icarus flew too close to the sun on wax wings made by his father Daedalus. His fall warns against hubris.

Myths answer questions science had not yet asked: why the seasons turn, why suffering exists, why kings rule. Icarus encodes its culture's answers in narrative form — explanations you can remember because they move you. Viewed through a contemporary-relevance lens, Icarus is brought into the present, where its patterns still appear in new clothes.

To ask what Icarus explains is to recover the curiosity that made it. A second sub-question concerns the historical kernel: what real events or places might stand behind Icarus. Related entries in this archive: The Furies and Shiva.
